A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HERMES and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary material. Matching relocated and renumbered content supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original scene-understanding, point-cloud generation, ablation, and trajectory-planning results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V3 retains original understanding and generation results, ablations, NuScenes-QA evaluation, and qualitative experiments.

M1.justification: V3 removes the auxiliary HERMES-p variant described in v2 Section A.4, including its ego-state inputs, trajectory-prediction MLP, and feedback of predicted trajectories into world queries. The central HERMES architecture and training objectives remain unchanged; the added opacity formula documents the existing renderer rather than establishing a changed procedure.

E1.justification: V3 removes the entire open-loop trajectory-planning task and the generation scenario using predicted future ego-motion, previously evaluated through HERMES-p. This substantively narrows task and scenario coverage. NuScenes, NuInteract, OmniDrive-nuScenes, and NuScenes-QA remain; the updated NuInteract citation does not establish a dataset change.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds separated unification to the main comparison, whereas v2 evaluated it only in Table 2's ablation. Removing Table A6 also eliminates the planning comparisons against UniAD, VAD-Base, and OccWorld-D. Together these change both the main control comparison and an entire category of comparators; retained specialist and NuScenes-QA comparator sets are unchanged.

E3.justification: The removed planning evaluation used trajectory L2 error and collision rate at 1–3 seconds and their averages, following BEV-Planner. V3 also adds a separated-unification control to the main evaluation. Retained dataset splits, generation and language metrics, quarter-data ablation settings, and training budgets are unchanged.

E4.justification: V3 removes the test of how generation behaves when predicted trajectories replace ground-truth future motion, while extending the separated-versus-unified analysis to the main comparison. The world-query, generation-length, pooling, BEV-size, model-scaling, query-count, controllability, and difficult-scene analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests. The revised tables retain the same point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: V3 removes HERMES-p results, including 3s Chamfer distance 1.48, and all planning outcomes in Table A6, including average L2 error 0.36 m and collision rate 0.32%. It adds separated-unification results in Table 1: 3s Chamfer distance 1.37 and CIDEr 0.745. Table 2's understanding-only METEOR changes from 0.377 to 0.379 and ROUGE from 0.321 to 0.323. Main HERMES scores remain unchanged, including 1.17 and 0.741 respectively; the new comparator row is not a same-method performance improvement.

T1.justification: Section 4.1 newly defines opacity from adjacent SDF values using a sigmoid with learnable parameter t; v2 only identifies alpha_i as opacity. Other equations remain mathematically equivalent, including the total loss after substituting the weights already specified in v2 Appendix A.1. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims of unifying 3D understanding and generation through BEV representations and world queries. The first-unified-world-model claim and reported 32.4% generation-error reduction and 8.0% CIDEr improvement are unchanged.

C2.justification: V3 removes the interpretation that predicted-trajectory errors cause an expected, acceptable generation degradation and the discussion of operating without known future vehicle motion. Section 5.2 instead discusses the new separated-unification comparison as evidence of cross-task knowledge transfer. Existing perception, image-generation, occlusion, turning, and nighttime limitations remain.

D1.justification: V3 supplies the renderer's opacity calculation and learnable sigmoid parameter, but removes HERMES-p implementation details and v2's explicit statement that default generation uses ground-truth future ego-motion. NuInteract's repository reference is replaced by a paper citation. Training details and the HERMES code-release promise remain unchanged; loss weights are merely moved into the main objective.

R1.justification: V3 adds background citations on temporal fusion, DDS3D, spectral-domain fine-tuning, and token compression, and removes the UniAD, VAD, and BEV-Planner references associated with planning. NuInteract's reference is updated. The related-work argument and novelty positioning remain substantially unchanged; expanded venue names are bibliographic presentation edits.

P1.justification: V3 locally shortens method descriptions, adds a causal-attention explanation, and rewrites part of Section 5.2. It removes the planning subsection, introduces a separate Supplementary Material heading with S-numbered sections, and adds corresponding-author and acknowledgment text. Most prose and the overall narrative sequence are retained.

P2.justification: V3 removes Table A6, swaps the placement of Figure 3 and Table 2, and relocates Figure A1 as Figure S1. Table 1 gains green highlighting, Figure 2 labels are refined, and some equations and captions are reformatted. The retained qualitative figures show the same examples rather than new visual evidence.

improvement.justification: V3 improves direct validation of unification through the added main comparator, makes Table 2 consistent with its stated 0.002 metric gaps, and clarifies the renderer mathematics. However, removing HERMES-p also removes the quantitative test of generation using predicted future motion, reducing evidence about that applicability condition. These substantive gains and losses leave the net effect on overall quality uncertain.
